Call from the user gesture: choose a Cloud copy or Private collection,
or create a collection in Connect. No current collection is preselected.

Call from the user gesture: re-approve the open (or requested) collection,
for example after access was lost or the app needs a wider grant.

Configure the open collection from the declaration, with nothing to review
(`setup.plan` + `setup.apply` is the reviewable form).

Sign out of mdbase on this device (see `MdbaseApplication.signOut`).
Rejects with `sign_out_pending_writes` while changes are still saving,
unless `{discard: true}`.

members.name: unsynced
members.signature: readonly unsynced: { /** Open the app's unsynced collection in this tab, creating it on first * use: for "Continue without connecting". Signed out with nothing * requested, `start()` already does this. */ open(options?: MdbaseApplicationRequestOptions): Promise<MdbaseSnapshot>; /** Compare the unsynced collection with the open (ready) collection: what * would be created, what an earlier transfer already brought, what `map` * leaves out, renamed paths and types the destination lacks. Writes nothing. */ planTransfer(options?: MdbaseTransferPlanOptions): Promise<MdbaseTransferPlan>; /** Create a plan's records in the open collection, keeping their IDs. * Interrupted? Ask the person to * confirm first: it cannot be undone. A tab showing it continues in a new, * empty one. */ discard(options?: MdbaseApplicationRequestOptions): Promise<MdbaseSnapshot>; }
members.description: Work before connecting (the `unsynced` option).

members.name: application
members.description: The underlying application, for code written against `MdbaseConnect`.

featured.name: MdbaseApplicationDeclaration

members.name: installationKind
members.description:
Installation kind sent at pairing; the origin must be declared under the
manifest's `installation_origins.<environment>.<kind>`. Default: "mobile"
for `capacitor://` origins, else "app-runtime". Android Capacitor apps
served from https set "mobile" explicitly.

members.name: manifest
members.description:
Complete canonical manifest data; runtime validation uses the public
Connect parser. Accepts canonical typed builders without index-signature casts.

members.name: followVisibility
members.description:
Drive `setForeground` from `document.visibilityState`, and sync at once
when the page regains focus or the network comes back. A hidden page only
finishes sending pending writes (for at most two minutes). Default true;
false leaves `setForeground` to the app.

members.name: readiness
members.description:
Readiness policy. `typeIssues: "degrade"` keeps the collection ready when
one of the app's own types has an error-level definition issue, and lists
it in `readiness.assessment.unavailableTypes`; the app must then treat
that type as unavailable. Default "block". Issues on definitions the app
does not declare never affect readiness.

members.name: privateCollections
members.description:
SDK-10: list this browser's Private collections (kept on the person's
computers) in `collections` and open them by the same selection. Default
true; false for an app that lists them itself through the app-grant entry.

members.name: unsynced
members.description:
Let people start working before they sign in or connect a collection.
Signed out with no collection requested, the app opens its unsynced
collection (`phase.kind === "unsynced"`): saved only in this browser,
never listed in `collections`. Default false.

featured.name: MdbaseSnapshot
featured.description: The application snapshot with the derived fields always present.

members.name: phase
members.description:
R1: the one derived state for UI. Switch on `phase.kind`; never hand-roll
a ready check from `status`/`readiness`. Always set by the SDK entry.

members.name: sync
members.description: Sync of the open collection (null until it is ready).

members.name: links
members.description: Connect pages for this account (SDK-4). Null where the SDK cannot run.

featured.name: MdbasePhase

members.name: records
members.description: Actual public borrowed UI client, not a legacy facade or second engine.

members.name: files
members.description: SAME records.files. Available accessors do not widen original authority.

members.name: status
members.description: `current`: nothing to do. `setup`: changes to apply. `conflict`: blocked.

members.name: digest
members.description: Binds the reviewed collection state and decisions.

members.name: summary
members.description: One plain sentence for the top of the review screen.

members.name: adoptable
members.description: Conflicts that using the app's version would resolve: pass as `adopt` and plan again.

members.name: staged
members.signature: readonly staged: readonly { readonly path: string; readonly document: string; }[]
members.description: The definition documents setup would write, for a details view.

members.name: records

members.name: refusal
members.signature: readonly refusal?: { readonly code: MdbaseSetupRefusalCode; readonly message: string; }

featured.name: MdbaseSetupResult
featured.description:
SDK-8: how `setup.apply` ended. `changed`: the collection changed since the
plan was reviewed (plan again). `unknown`: the result is not known yet; the
snapshot settles it. Refusals and other failures still reject.

featured.name: MdbaseAccessRequest
featured.description: What an app asks for at the moment of use. Only file actions today.

featured.name: MdbaseAccessResult
featured.description:
`granted`: the open collection's connection may now use `actions` (every
file action it is allowed, reads included). `declined`: the person said no.
`cancelled`: the window was closed, the request expired or was aborted.

members.name: source
members.description: The unsynced collection.

members.name: missingTypes
members.description:
Types the records to create name that the destination does not define
and this transfer does not add. They are still created; the app may ask
the person to add the types, or plan again with `addTypes`.

members.name: addTypes
members.description:
Types the transfer adds to the destination, from the source's own
definitions (`addTypes` only).

members.name: counts
members.signature: readonly counts: Readonly<{ create: number; present: number; skipped: number; renamed: number; changed: number; }>

members.name: app
members.description: App ID and version, sent in `hello`.

members.name: timezone
members.description: IANA time zone for this session's writes and queries. Defaults to the host's.

members.name: features
members.description: Extra features to request ("fence", "presence", ...).

members.name: reconnect
members.signature: reconnect?: false | { minDelayMs?: number; maxDelayMs?: number; }
members.description: Reconnect after the link drops (default on).

members.name: waitForDevice
members.description: Private collections: wait for a device replica to come online instead of failing.

members.name: onWaiting
members.description: Called while waiting for a device or the original Native grant to become live.

members.name: ledger
members.description: Where the write ledger persists (default: memory). Web apps get the replica's store.

members.name: files
members.description: Files: handles, uploads, downloads (§10).

members.name: presence
members.description: Presence on records (§11).

members.name: ledger
members.description:
Unconfirmed and refused writes, and the overall save state. Survives a
reload when the connector persists it (web apps do). Event-driven: it
settles from receipts and the replica's status push, never by polling.

members.name: connect
members.description:
Connect to a replica and say hello. With `waitForDevice`, a private collection with
no device online keeps retrying (calling `onWaiting`) instead of failing.
A next-relay pre-live grant waits up to 30 seconds on this same connector.
This is initial hello only: no application request or unknown write is replayed.

members.name: hello
members.description: The negotiated session, with its latest role-effective grant.

members.name: linkProblem
members.description:
Why the link is not open: the last connect error. `reason: "no_device_online"`
means a private collection has no device replica reachable right now; show
"waiting for one of your devices" rather than an error.

members.name: onLink
members.signature: onLink(fn: (s: LinkState, why: MdbaseError | null) => void): () => void

members.name: readFenced
members.description: Next-relay consistency floor ONLY; not keyed/readable/Saved authority.

members.name: readyForRead
members.description: Recheck session identity after waiting for catch-up (SDK-internal use).

members.name: currentSession
members.description: The open session, or throw `unavailable` (SDK-internal use).

members.name: call
members.signature: call<T = CborValue>(method: string, p: CborValue, o?: { signal?: AbortSignal; codec?: import("./codec.js").Codec<T>; retry?: boolean; }): Promise<T>
members.description:
Advanced: run a request on the current session; on a dropped link, wait for the
reconnect and retry when `retry` (idempotent requests only).

members.name: authenticatedDevice
members.description:
Transport-authenticated replica identity (Noise target), NOT hello/witness
self-claims. Absent when the transport has no authenticated device identity.

members.name: headWitness
members.description: The replica's latest signed head witness from `hello`, if it sent one.

members.name: status
members.description: The latest known status.

members.name: getStatus
members.description: Fresh status from the replica.

members.name: appliedPrefix
members.description:
Read the retained historical chain at a captured hosted fence. READ/session
authorization is unchanged. No automatic retry/reconnect: a handover must
revalidate the authenticated session and all readiness gates after any await.
Missing chain or any error means remain hosted; never substitute asOf or the
current head/generations. Decoding does not authenticate a witness or switch.

members.name: onStatus
members.description: Call `fn` with the status now and on every change (pushed, ≤ 4/s).

members.name: describe
members.description:
Catalog summary: types with their version, source revision and contract
implementations, contracts, settings (§4.4). `definitions` adds each type's
definition and schema and each contract's schemas, bounded by the replica
(`too_large` when over budget; read them with `resources.get` instead).
A producer that cannot describe definitions fails `upgrade_required`.

members.name: createType
members.description:
Create a type from its complete type-file `document`. The replica's Core
derives the name and path (`<types_folder>/<name>.md`) from the local
catalog, then the document is written create-only there, so a concurrent
creator loses with `conflict`. Refusals: `invalid_record` /
`invalid_type_definition` (unusable name, or the definition is invalid
when written), `conflict` / `type_conflict` (the name exists under any
casing) or `path_taken`, and `forbidden` without `definitions.manage`.
Update a type with `resources.put(path, document, { baseRevision })`,
using the path and revision from `describe`.

members.name: describeTyping
members.signature: describeTyping(types: readonly string[], paths: readonly string[], signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<DescribeTypingResult>
members.description:
Core's temporal typing for top-level fields under a query's exact `types` OR list
(`date` / `date_time` only when every type agrees; otherwise `none`). The answer is
bound to a catalog generation; nested paths are `none`. The SDK never infers typing.

members.name: get
members.signature: get(ref: RecordRef, include?: Include, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<RecordView>
members.description: One record by ID or path. Throws `not_found`.

members.name: getContract
members.signature: getContract(ref: RecordRef, contract: ContractSelector, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ContractRecordView>
members.description:
One record's valid view through a record contract, mapped by the replica's
Core. Refusals: `not_found` (no record, or `data_contract_not_implemented`
when it does not implement the contract), `not_found`/`data_contract_not_found`,
`invalid_request`/`data_contract_ambiguous` (select `type`; details: the types),
`invalid_record`/`data_contract_record_invalid` (with issues), and
`upgrade_required`/`contract_records_unsupported` from an older replica.

members.name: readMany
members.signature: readMany(refs: readonly RecordRef[], include?: Include, signal?: AbortSignal, options?: ReadManyOptions): Promise<RecordView[]>
members.description:
Bounded ordered ordinary gets. Missing/refused reads fail the batch;
duplicate slots and the original signal are retained, not a snapshot.

members.name: find
members.signature: find(ref: RecordRef, include?: Include, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<RecordView | null>
members.description: One record, or `null` when there is none.

members.name: query
members.signature: query(query: Query, include?: Include, signal?: AbortSignal, opts?: { contract?: string; }): Promise<QueryResult>
members.description:
One page of a query, evaluated by the replica (body predicates and links
included, §4). Pass `result.cursor` back as `query.cursor` for the next.
`opts.contract` is not supported by the live replica dispatch. Supplying it
returns `invalid_request` with reason `unknown_param`; no contract filter
is applied. The option remains encoded unchanged for API compatibility.

members.name: queryContract
members.description:
Canonical contract projections with validation issues and ordinary cursor
metadata. Positive page sizes above the producer's 128-record maximum clamp
to 128; use the returned cursor for the remaining records. Old producers
refuse; there is no SDK projection fallback.

members.name: backlinks
members.signature: backlinks(target: RecordRef, o?: { include?: Include; limit?: number; cursor?: string; signal?: AbortSignal; }): Promise<BacklinksResult>
members.description:
One page of the records whose links resolve to `target`, from the
replica's link index with Core resolution over the local view (pending
changes included; the target's links to itself excluded). Referrers come
in path order, each with its links to the target. Pass the returned
`cursor` for the next page (`limit` 1–1000, default 128); a page may hold
fewer than `limit`, and only an absent cursor ends the list. Any local
change between pages refuses the continuation with `cursor_stale`: start
again from the first page. A replica without the method refuses with
`upgrade_required` / `backlinks_unsupported` (§4.2).

members.name: resolveLinks
members.signature: resolveLinks(from: string, links: readonly string[], o?: { signal?: AbortSignal; }): Promise<ResolveLinksResult>
members.description:
Resolve link occurrences written in the note at `from`, exactly as the
replica resolves them for backlinks and rename: Core parsing and spec 08
resolution over the local view, pending changes included. `from` need not
exist yet (an unsaved draft). Each entry is one occurrence as written —
`[[target]]`, `![[target#anchor|alias]]`, `[text](path)`, `![alt](path)` —
and the result holds one resolution per entry, in order: a record or file
with its ID and path, `ambiguous` with sorted candidate paths, or
`not_found` / `invalid`. Titles and aliases are not link keys. 1–512
entries of at most 4096 bytes each. A replica without the method refuses
with `upgrade_required` / `resolve_links_unsupported` (§4.3).

members.name: resources
members.signature: readonly resources: { get: (path: string, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<ResourceView>; /** One bounded resource inventory page. Text defaults to false; limit defaults * to 64 (maximum 128). Preserve folder/text/limit on continuation. Collect all * pages before assessing a complete snapshot; stale/expired cursors require * explicit reassessment, never an automatic restart. */ list: (o?: { folder?: string; text?: boolean; cursor?: string; limit?: number; signal?: AbortSignal; }) => Promise<import("./wire.js").ListResourcesResult>; /** * Write a resource. CAS: pass the revision you read as `baseRevision`, or * `mustNotExist` to create only (a taken path is `conflict` / `path_taken`). Not both. */ put: (path: string, doc: string, o?: WriteOptions & { baseRevision?: string; mustNotExist?: boolean; }) => Promise<Write>; delete: (path: string, o?: WriteOptions & { baseRevision?: string; }) => Promise<Write>; }
members.description: Definitions: `mdbase.yaml`, type files, contract files (§4.1).

members.name: typePacks
members.signature: readonly typePacks: Readonly<{ plan: (pack: TypePackProvision, options: TypePackOptions) => Promise<TypePackPlan>; apply: (plan: TypePackPlan, o?: WriteOptions) => Promise<TypePackApplyResult>; }>
members.description:
Type packs: `plan` (writes nothing), review, then `apply(plan)` as one
guarded all-or-nothing mutation (needs `definitions.manage`).

members.name: views
members.signature: readonly views: { createSource: (input: ViewSourceCreateInput, options: ViewSourceWriteOptions) => Promise<Write>; updateSource: (seen: RecordView, document: string, options: ViewSourceWriteOptions) => Promise<Write>; getSourceRecord: (source: RecordRef, options?: ViewSourceReadOptions) => Promise<RecordView>; /** `mdbase.view` sources (spec 12 `list_views` shape), resolved over served * contract queries: the native runtime has no `list_views` RPC. */ list: (folder?: string, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<ListViewsResult>; /** Spec 11 named-view resolution, executed as one ordinary native query. */ execute: (source: RecordRef, view: string, o?: ExecuteViewOptions) => Promise<QueryResult>; readSource: (source: RecordRef, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<ViewSourceDocument>; }
members.description:
Saved views (§4.3). Source helpers use ordinary record ops/full CAS reads;
web app-host Bases reads use the separate native AppBases methods.

members.name: pendingWrites
members.description:
Pending mutations of this session's owner (its grant, or the device), oldest
first (§6): a new session after a reload sees writes made before it. Follow
each with `awaitReceipt`, or keep the `mutationId` you chose and call
`receipt(id)` / `awaitReceipt(id)`. Pages through everything.

members.name: preflightRename
members.signature: preflightRename(target: RecordView, to: string, o?: { updateRefs?: boolean; }): Promise<Preflight>
members.description:
What a rename would do to links (dry run, §5): the rewrites, and links left broken.
Throws the problem the real rename would get.

members.name: preflightDelete
members.description: Links a delete would break (dry run, §5).

members.name: pages
members.signature: pages(query: Query, include?: Include, signal?: AbortSignal, options?: PagesOptions): AsyncGenerator<QueryResult>
members.description:
Every page of a query. Cursor resets require explicit caller clearing;
otherwise cursor_expired/cursor_stale is thrown unchanged.

members.name: queryPages
members.signature: queryPages(query: Query, include?: Include, signal?: AbortSignal, options?: PagesOptions): AsyncGenerator<QueryResult>
members.description: Shared alias of pages(): whole native pages, no implicit cursor reset.

members.name: live
members.description:
A live query. Subscribe for pushes; keep lists cheap with a `limit` window and no
bodies, and widen the window with `setQuery`.

members.name: changes
members.signature: changes(cursor?: string, limit?: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<ChangesResult>
members.description: One page of the change feed. A `reset: true` result means "re-read what you cache".

members.name: watchChanges
members.signature: watchChanges(cursor: string | undefined, onChanges: (batch: ChangesResult) => void): ChangesWatch
members.description:
Follow the change feed from `cursor`. `onChanges` gets every batch; `reset: true`
means the app must re-read what it caches. Survives reconnects.
`ready` confirms the first watch ACK, not a complete/current collection cache.
After reconnect, observe `state`; an already-resolved promise is not freshness.

members.name: validate
members.signature: validate(refs?: readonly RecordRef[], signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<RecordValidation[]>
members.description:
Validate these records, or every record. Every record is validated a
page at a time when the replica grants `validate-page-v1`; each page is an
independent READ, so records changed meanwhile may be missed or repeated.
Older replicas validate every record in one bounded request.

members.name: executeAppBases
members.description:
Independent native app-host Bases READ, exact original held session.
Unsupported transports refuse: no generic execute_view/data fallback.

members.name: executeAppBasesPages
members.signature: executeAppBasesPages(request: AppBasesRequest, options?: AppBasesPagesOptions): AsyncGenerator<{ kind: "refusal"; problem: Problem; } | import("./app-host/bases-pages.js").AppBasesPage, any, any>
members.description:
All rows of a saved view, page by page over native windows (prod
`executeViewPages`). Each page is an independent READ; `changedSinceFirst`
marks pages taken after the collection changed.

members.name: listAppBasesViews
members.description:
One bounded native discovery page. Empty views do not mean EOF when a
continuation is present. Supplied handles never silently restart/retry.

members.name: readAppBasesViewSource
members.description:
Exact current source for one native UUID/SHA/original ordinal, never path
aliases, inferred catalog entries, generic RPC or cached document fallback.

members.name: submit
members.signature: submit(ops: Op[], o?: WriteOptions & { allowPartial?: boolean; }): Promise<Write[]>
members.description: Submit operations as one mutation (or one per op with `allowPartial`).

members.name: create
members.description: Create a record. The ID is minted here, so the app can use it before confirmation.

members.name: update
members.signature: update(target: RecordRef, changes: UpdateInput, o?: WriteOptions): Promise<Write>
members.description:
Update a record by field-level intent. Pass the `RecordView` you edited from, and
the SDK sends `base` for every key you set or unset, and the body as a 3-way merge,
so concurrent edits merge instead of last-writer-wins.

members.name: updateOp
members.signature: updateOp(target: RecordRef, c: UpdateInput): Op & { kind: "update"; }
members.description: Build an `update` op (exposed for batching with `submit`).

members.name: replaceDocument
members.signature: replaceDocument(target: RecordRef, document: string, o?: WriteOptions & { ifRevision?: string; }): Promise<Write>
members.description: Replace a record's whole document.

members.name: delete
members.signature: delete(target: RecordRef, o?: WriteOptions & { ifRevision?: string; contract?: ContractSelector; }): Promise<Write>
members.description:
Delete a record. With a RecordView, a concurrent change supersedes the delete.
With `contract`, the record must implement it; the delete is then bound to
the revision checked, so a concurrent change supersedes it.

members.name: rename
members.signature: rename(target: RecordView | ContractRecordView, to: string, o?: WriteOptions & { updateRefs?: boolean; ifRevision?: string; contract?: ContractSelector; }): Promise<Write>
members.description:
Rename (move) a record; `updateRefs` rewrites links to it (default true).
With `contract`, the record must implement it, and moves from its current path.

members.name: save
members.signature: save(write: Write | Promise<Write>, o?: { readBack?: boolean; timeoutMs?: number; signal?: AbortSignal; }): Promise<SaveResult>
members.description:
Settle a write for the UI: waits up to `timeoutMs` (default 3 s) for the log
to confirm it. Still pending then is `saved_on_device`, not a failure: the
write is kept on this device and the ledger settles it later. With
`readBack`, `record` is the record as it now reads here.

members.name: receipt
members.description: The current receipt of a mutation. Failures carry `mutationId`.

members.name: awaitReceipt
members.signature: awaitReceipt(mutation: Uuid, timeoutMs?: number, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Receipt>
members.description: Resolves when the receipt leaves `pending`, or at `timeoutMs` with the pending receipt.

members.name: onHolds
members.description: Call `fn` with the holds now and on every change.

members.name: resolveHold
members.signature: resolveHold(id: Uuid, how: HoldResolution, use?: string): Promise<Write>
members.description: Resolve a hold. Submits an ordinary mutation and returns its write.

members.name: dismissConflict
members.description: Accept what the record kept.

members.name: resolveConflict
members.signature: resolveConflict(entry: ConflictEntry, field: string, chosen: PlainValue, o?: WriteOptions): Promise<Write>
members.description: Resolve a field conflict with a chosen value, dismissing it in the same mutation.

members.name: pendingDevices
members.description:
Devices waiting for approval in a private collection. Offered only to the app
hosting the replica (no grant). `exchangeReady` is challenge/reveal readiness,
NOT approval/key delivery. Once ready, `sas` is the host-only comparison code
to display beside Allow; the user must check it matches on the other computer.

members.name: approveDevice
members.description:
Confirm with the six digits displayed for the current host exchange, only
after the user visually checks they match on the requesting computer. Nothing
is typed. Never substitute a newer code after the user confirms. The replica
checks the current context and awaits the actual approval disposition.

members.name: rejectDevice
members.description: Dismiss this request until a fresh commitment is logged, including automatic renewal. Not revocation.

members.name: accountKey
members.signature: readonly accountKey: { /** Setup step 2: check the enrolment and key the recovery device (an ordinary mutation). */ setup: (secret: Uint8Array) => Promise<Write>; /** Unlock step 3: start the recovery-signed self-grant; poll `status` until `keyed` or `refused`. */ unlock: (secret: Uint8Array) => Promise<void>; status: (signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<AccountKeyStatus>; }
members.description:
The account key (AK1 §6; hosting app only, never over a cloud-copy thin session).
`secret` is the 32-byte account secret `R`; the replica derives the collection's
recovery device from it and drops it. The SDK keeps no copy.

members.name: recoveryKey
members.signature: readonly recoveryKey: { /** Whether a recovery key is set up for this collection. */ status: () => Promise<RecoveryKeyStatus>; /** * Create a recovery key. The returned phrase is shown to the user once and never * stored by the SDK; the replica keys a recovery device with it. */ create: () => Promise<{ phrase: string; device: Uuid; }>; /** Join this device using a recovery phrase (when no other device is available). */ import: (phrase: string) => Promise<void>; }
members.description: Recovery key for a private collection (hosting app only).

members.name: offerFence
members.description:
Offer the editor fence: the replica will route changes to open files through
`handler`. Requires the "fence" feature in `hello`.

members.name: reportFence
members.description: Report the files open in editors (on open, close, dirty change, and after saves).

featured.name: Query
featured.description: A spec 11 query object. Plain objects are converted to data maps.

members.name: id
members.description: A record ID minted by the caller; default a new UUIDv7.

members.name: frontmatter
members.signature: frontmatter?: Map<string, PlainValue> | { [k: string]: PlainValue | undefined; }

members.name: document
members.description: Complete source instead of frontmatter + body.

members.name: contract
members.description:
Create through a record contract: `frontmatter` holds contract fields, which
the replica maps to the implementing type's record fields (and sets `type`).
Unmapped contract fields and an invalid resulting view are refused before
anything is submitted. Not with `document`.

members.name: updateRefs
members.description: Rewrite inbound links on path-stored field moves (default true).

members.name: patch
members.signature: patch?: Map<string, PlainValue> | { [k: string]: PlainValue | undefined; }
members.description: Set these top-level keys.

members.name: body
members.description: Replace the body. With a RecordView target, it is sent as a 3-way merge.

members.name: ifRevision
members.description: Opt-in whole-document CAS.

members.name: contract
members.description:
Update through a record contract: `patch` and `unset` name contract fields,
mapped by the replica to record fields (nested record fields are merged with
the current record, sending their observed values as `base`). The record
must implement the contract. `patch`, `unset`, the body options and `ifRevision`
apply, in one atomic update.

members.name: promote
members.description:
With `contract`: an untyped record (no type membership) first takes the
selected implementing type through the collection's explicit type key, in
the same atomic update; its ID, body and other fields are kept. A record
that already implements the contract is updated as usual; one with other
types is refused (`invalid_request`/`data_contract_promote_typed`). Older
replicas refuse the option with `invalid_request`.

members.name: intent
members.description:
A stable name for this one write, such as a draft ID. Retrying with the same
`intent` in the same collection sends the same mutation (and, for `create`,
the same record ID), so a write retried after a lost reply lands once; the
first attempt's content wins. Use a new name for each new write.

members.name: wait
members.description: Hold for log confirmation, or final local file publication (not confirmation).

members.name: validation
members.description:
Validation level for this write's single-record checks (spec 04); default
the collection's `settings.validation`. Only `error` refuses a write with
`invalid_record`. A sync tool sends `warn`: files it carries are never
rejected for validity. Older replicas ignore it and refuse at `error`.

featured.name: Write
featured.description:
A submitted write. `receipt` is what the replica answered (usually `pending` with
optimistic `records`). `confirmed` settles when it leaves `pending`.

members.name: confirmed
members.description: Resolves with the confirmed receipt; rejects with the problem if rejected or unknown.

members.name: published
members.description:
Final local file result, possibly BEFORE log confirmation. `not_published`
is a final non-publication, not success. Without files, settles at confirmation.
Rejects rejected/unknown outcomes; not a native custody/durable ACK gate.

members.name: records
members.description: The records as they now read locally (optimistic until confirmed).

members.name: update
members.description: SDK-internal: apply a newer receipt. Kept in the published types (apps' tests use it).

members.name: record
members.description: The first record, read back when asked.

members.name: ready
members.description: Rejects if the first subscribe fails; resolves on the first snapshot.

members.name: error

members.name: records

members.name: stale
